title: Open problem: dimension of posets with planar cover graphs vs. height
statement_text: It is not known whether the dimension of posets with planar cover graphs is bounded by a linear function of their height (or any polynomial function for that matter).
context_text: Posets are finite. The dimension $\dim(P)$ of a poset $P$ is the least integer $d$ such that $P$ is the intersection of $d$ linear orders (linear extensions of $P$). A chain is a set of pairwise comparable elements, and the height of $P$ is the maximum size of a chain. A relation $a<b$ is a cover relation if there is no $c$ with $a<c<b$; the cover graph of $P$ is the undirected graph on the elements of $P$ whose edges are the cover relations, i.e. the (Hasse) diagram seen as an undirected graph. $P$ is a planar poset if its diagram can be drawn in the plane without crossings with every cover relation $a<b$ drawn as a curve going upwards from $a$ to $b$; planar posets have planar cover graphs, but for every $h\ge3$ there are non-planar posets of height $h$ with planar cover graphs. The paper's main result is that every planar poset of height $h$ has dimension at most $192h+96$, while Kelly's construction shows that planar posets of height $h$ can have dimension about $h$, so a linear bound is optimal up to a constant factor. By a theorem of Streib and Trotter, the dimension of posets with planar cover graphs is bounded by some function of the height, but the known bound is exponential. The authors also construct posets of height $h$ with planar cover graphs and dimension at least $2h-2$, and show that planarity is essential: there are posets whose cover graphs exclude $K_5$ as a minor with dimension at least $2^{h/2}$ for height $h$.
notes: Stated in running prose without a labelled theorem environment; clearly identified as an open problem by the authors.
paper_title: Planar posets have dimension at most linear in their height
